title: Building an offer that justifies a higher rate for Pressure cleaning (all heights)
audience: Owners and crew leads in pressure cleaning who quote driveways, paths, house exteriors and decks, including solo operators.
learningOutcomes: Write a pressure cleaning offer with a clear result, the surfaces named, time frame, conditions and fix-first promise
Identify the friction and risk the customer carries, such as runoff, height and what is excluded, and reduce them
Price a pressure cleaning package on value, surface and storey, then check it against your own hours

instruction.heading: What a pressure cleaning customer buys
instruction.body: A pressure cleaning customer buys a driveway, path or house exterior that looks clean across the whole area quoted, with the surfaces named and the limits clear. 'I will pressure wash your driveway' names a task. 'I will clean the driveway and the front path that I measured at the site visit, and I will not clean the solar panels or the roof' names the result and the limits. The limits protect the price.

instruction.heading: Packages that step up, and what the price evidence can bear
instruction.body: Use three tiers: driveway; driveway and front path; driveway, path and house exterior, with the storey stated. Stepped packages are one way to present an offer (Jobber Academy, May 2021, updated 8 October 2024), though its examples are not pressure cleaning. The price evidence is from What's The Damage, a lead-generation guide. It gives a standard driveway at $150 to $400, typical $250; a concrete path at $100 to $220, typical $140; a single-storey house exterior at $250 to $700, typical $420; a double-storey exterior at $450 to $1,100, typical $750; and a deck or patio at $150 to $450, typical $280. The guide says quotes without a site visit are estimates. Read these as a reference band, not an average, and build your tiers from your own measured area and hours, as set out in the pressure BP-05 lesson.

instruction.heading: Storey and surface are visible lines
instruction.body: The guide gives no percentage for a second storey. It puts the typical double-storey exterior $330 above the single-storey typical, which is a derived difference ($750 less $420). Show the storey as its own line, with the reason. The guide says pressure washing is priced by surface and area but gives no per-square-metre figure, so this research does not support a per-square-metre rate. Measure the area at the site visit and state it on the quote.

instruction.heading: One total, with GST stated
instruction.body: Show the all-in total for each package and say whether GST is included. The ACCC says misleading statements about prices are prohibited (last modified 15 July 2026). Hidden add-ons, such as a surcharge that appears only at invoice, undermine a higher rate, so put every line on the quote.

instruction.heading: Runoff is part of the offer, and the rule needs checking
instruction.body: Runoff from a driveway or house wash can reach stormwater. EPA Victoria's fact sheet on car repair says that discharging industrial waste to stormwater is an offence and that the regulator can prosecute. That sheet is about car repair and says it does not cover washing outdoor surfaces, so it does not set the rule for driveway or house washing. An EPA Victoria release reviewed on 13 June 2024 shows the regulator acting on a soap manufacturer's discharge: over 1,000 litres to a stormwater drain, with a fine of $9,616. That was not a cleaning business, but it shows that drain discharges are enforced. Before you wash near a drain, check the runoff rule with EPA Victoria, and state in the offer how water is controlled.

instruction.heading: Keep solar panels out of a house-wash package
instruction.body: Solar Victoria says not to use a pressure hose on panels and not to use harsh soap or chemicals; water is usually enough. If the same crew is booked for house washing and panels, keep them as separate lines, and say in the offer that panels are excluded from a pressure package.

instruction.heading: Guarantees, results and height
instruction.body: Do not state a stain-removal result you have not shown. Consumer Victoria says a business should be given a reasonable chance to fix a minor fault free of charge, though the page sets no fix window; publish one you can keep. Work from a ladder or pole on a double-storey house is work at height. The Commonwealth falls code (registered 2016) says ladders are for access and that a platform or scaffold should be considered first. That code is not Victorian law. Victoria was not checked for this draft, so check the Victorian rule with WorkSafe Victoria before you quote any storey.

procedure: Write the outcome in one sentence a customer would repeat, naming the surfaces and the limits.
Measure each surface at the site visit, and record the storey and access for each.
Build three tiers, price each from your own hours and the storey line, then check the totals against the lead-generation bands.
Write the water and runoff method for the site, and check the EPA Victoria rule before washing near a drain.
Name the exclusions, including solar panels and roofs unless they are separately quoted and checked.
Decide the fix-first window and check that you can keep it.
Show one all-in total for each tier and state whether GST is included.

workedExamples.situation: A single-storey house with a driveway and a front path. The client wants 'the whole outside done' and has not said whether the solar panels are included. The owner has not measured the surfaces.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Which tiers should the owner offer, and what should the quote say about the storey, the panels and the runoff?
workedExamples.reasoning: The owner offers three tiers, with the surfaces named from a measured site visit. Panels and roofs are listed as exclusions, and the storey line is shown. As a reference only, a driveway at the lead-generation typical of $250 and a single-storey house exterior at its typical of $420 add up to $670. That sum of two typicals is not a price for this house. The quote should come from measured area and the owner's own hours. Runoff is covered by the method, and the owner checks the EPA Victoria rule before washing near a drain.

equipmentAndPpe: Package sheet with three tiers and the all-in total
Measured area sheet for each surface, with storey and access
Water and runoff method for each site
Equipment for access and height as the Victorian working-at-height method requires; PPE as listed in {{business:safety.required_ppe}}

commonErrors.error: Quoting per surface with no measurements, so the client cannot see what is covered
commonErrors.prevention: Measure at the site visit and name each surface and its area on the quote.

commonErrors.error: Treating a lead-generation typical as the local average
commonErrors.prevention: Use the band as a reference only. The lead-generation guide says its figures are estimates and quotes without a site visit are estimates too.

commonErrors.error: Including solar panels or a roof in a house-wash package without checking the rule
commonErrors.prevention: Exclude panels from a pressure package, and check the Victorian rule before any roof work.

commonErrors.error: Promising a stain result you have not shown
commonErrors.prevention: Use only results you have photographed before and after.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Business guidance only. This lesson does not grant any licence. Victoria's working-at-height rules were not checked. The Commonwealth falls code and the NSW falls code are cited elsewhere and are not Victorian rules. Check the Victorian rule with WorkSafe Victoria before quoting any storey.

Runoff: the EPA Victoria car-repair sheet says that discharging industrial waste to stormwater is an offence, but it does not cover washing outdoor surfaces. Check the runoff rule for house and driveway washing with EPA Victoria before work near drains.
The ACCC says misleading price statements are prohibited, so the all-in total and GST status belong on every quote.

qualityStandard: Every pressure cleaning quote names the surfaces, the measured areas, the storey, the exclusions and an all-in total with GST status.
Every site has a recorded water and runoff method, checked against the EPA Victoria rule before washing near a drain.
No result is promised that the business has not shown.
documentationEvidence: Package sheet with the three tiers and the date it was set
Measured area and storey record for each site
Runoff method record, with the date it was checked
summary: A pressure cleaning customer buys a named result and clear limits.
Use lead-generation bands as a reference, not an average, and measure the area yourself.
Runoff, storeys and solar panels are visible lines, and each is checked against the Victorian rule before quoting.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which part of an offer does the pressure cleaning customer buy?
options: The clean surfaces named on the quote, with the limits stated

knowledgeChecks.question: What should a guarantee be?
options: Impossible to claim on in any case
Only for new customers and friends
Something you can deliver and afford

officialReferences.title: Setting prices: what's allowed (ACCC)
officialReferences.covers: Taken from the SOL-03 research file (tactic 11); the page was not reopened for this variant. Misleading price statements are prohibited, and an all-in price with GST status is the safer presentation. Publisher: ACCC.

sourceReferences: What's The Damage, 'Pressure washing cost guide', https://whatsthedamage.com.au/pressure-washing-cost/, verified November 2026, metadata 2026-11-01. Lead-generation guide; estimates, not measured; a site visit is needed for an accurate quote.

Jobber Academy, 'Good, Better, Best Pricing Examples', https://getjobber.com/academy/good-better-best-pricing-examples/, published May 2021, updated 8 October 2024. Older source. Supports: stepped packages.
INSEAD Knowledge, 'Small Change, Big Rewards', https://knowledge.insead.edu/marketing/small-change-big-rewards, 2 October 2025. Non-trade study.
ACCC, 'Setting prices: what's allowed', https://www.accc.gov.au/business/pricing/setting-prices-whats-allowed, last modified 15 July 2026. Supports: misleading price statements are prohibited.

Business Queensland, 'Preparing a business quote: tips', https://www.business.qld.gov.au/running-business/marketing-sales/sales/preparing-quote/tips, last updated 16 November 2022. Supports: add-ons and alternatives shown as separate lines on the quote.

Consumer Victoria, 'Services not done with due care and skill', https://www.consumer.vic.gov.au/products-and-services/problem-with-a-service/services-not-done-with-due-care-and-skill, last updated 13 October 2023. Supports: a reasonable chance to fix a minor fault; no fix window given.
Solar Victoria, 'Maintenance guide', https://www.solar.vic.gov.au/maintenance-guide, updated 17 July 2026. Supports: do not use a pressure hose on panels; water is usually enough.

EPA Victoria, 'Stormwater management for car repair industry', publication 1333.1, March 2015, https://www.epa.vic.gov.au/-/media/epa/files/publications/1333-1.pdf. Car-repair sheet; does not cover washing outdoor surfaces; Act citation from 1970 to be checked.

EPA Victoria, media release on a soap manufacturer's discharge, reviewed 13 June 2024, https://epa.vic.gov.au/about-epa/news-media-and-updates/media-releases-and-news/discharging-soap-leaves-a-stain. Not a cleaning business.

Work Health and Safety (Managing the Risk of Falls at Workplaces) Code of Practice 2015, https://legislation.gov.au/F2016L00425/asmade/2016-03-30/text/original/epub/OEBPS/document_1/document_1.html, registered 2016. Commonwealth code; not Victorian law.

Consumer Victoria, 'What is an owners corporation?', https://www.consumer.vic.gov.au/housing/owners-corporations/buying-into-an-owners-corporation/what-is-an-owners-corporation, updated 9 April 2026. Lists driveways, pathways, walls, stairwells and gardens as examples of common property, subject to the plan.
Note: Victorian OHS rules were not checked. Gaps: no per-square-metre price, no minimum charge and no real posted pressure-cleaning job was found.
